newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-RUSSIAN-BORN SKIER RAISES ISRAELI HOPES.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-RUSSIAN-BORN SKIER RAISES ISRAELI HOPES.

text.p: Vladimir Tupitsyn is a serious man with serious ambition.
The Russian-born athlete has dedicated his life to Nordic skiing and now has his chance on the international stage as Israel's first-ever competitor at World championship level.

Blond, blue-eyed Tupitsyn, 28, who emigrated to Israel four years ago, walked out alone carrying the Israeli flag at the opening ceremony of the 1997 Nordic skiing World championships on Thursday in the ancient city of Trondheim in mid-Norway.
"I felt very proud to be an Israeli and to carry the flag," Tupitsyn, who speaks Russian and Hebrew, said through his interpreter and manager Amir Kazenelson.
"The Norwegians are very, very friendly. When I'm skiing I hear them calling 'Hello Israel, hello Israel'."
Tupitsyn, married with a son, attended a special school for Nordic skiing in a suburb of Moscow from the age of 12 before competing at national level.

After his move to Israel, he spent two years out of the sport before finding funding from the Israeli ski federation and the Ministry of Sport. Now he trains in Europe and hopes to recover his lost form.

So far this year, Tupitsyn, a freestyle specialist, has notched up a sixth placing in the Scandinavian Cup 50 km freestyle in Lahti, Finland. In the first event of the World championships, the 30 km freestyle on Friday, he came in 86th out of 91 finishers.
"He is devoted to Nordic skiing. He is very precise in his training and diet. We hope he will be successful," Kazenelson said.
